findings.title: [P1] Restore socket listener detachment
findings.body: After a caller invokes the returned disposer, subsequent messages still reach the supposedly detached handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers and captured state, causing duplicate processing and unbounded listener growth.

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body: After teardown, `refresh` continues running every second. Repeated start/cleanup cycles accumulate concurrent pollers, retain callback state, and can prevent a Node.js process from exiting naturally.

findings.title: [P1] Restore socket listener detachment
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer removes the `"message"` listener. Any later message still invokes a supposedly disposed handler, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners and duplicate side effects.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval during disposal
findings.body:
The returned disposer leaves the interval active. After teardown, `refresh` continues running every second; repeated starts accumulate concurrent pollers, and in Node.js the referenced timer can also prevent process shutdown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned teardown no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. Any socket emitting afterward invokes stale handlers, causing duplicate processing and retained resources across reconnects or component disposal.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval during teardown
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup leaves the interval active. Disposed consumers continue refreshing every second, retained timers can keep Node processes or tests alive, and repeated starts accumulate concurrent polling loops.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore message-listener removal on disposal
findings.body:
The returned disposer no longer removes the listener. After disposal, an EventEmitter-style socket can still deliver attacker-controlled messages to a stale session handler; repeated attach/dispose cycles also retain handlers and their captured state indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation on disposal
findings.body:
Every call now creates a permanent interval. In a long-running service where reconnects or request lifecycles repeatedly start and dispose polling, callbacks and captured state accumulate without bound, enabling resource exhaustion and multiplying any work performed by `refresh`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Detach the message handler in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
On a long-lived socket, every attach/cleanup cycle permanently retains another handler. Repeated lifecycle operations cause unbounded listener and captured-memory growth, duplicate work per message, and eventual listener-limit warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup no longer stops polling. Each cycle leaves a timer and callback alive forever, causing accumulating periodic work and preventing a Node.js process from exiting naturally after polling has supposedly stopped.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
